plan.title: 4 tips for your first time
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Read the Crew Roles script word for word the first time. It's written to land.
Explain AI as "a friend who's never seen the picture." The clearer the words, the better the result.
If a pair gets stuck, suggest one change: add a color word, or say where things are.
Don't fix their prompts. The struggle is the lesson.

warmup.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Read the role scripts word for word the first time.
Call the AI "a friend who's never seen the picture."
If a pair is stuck, suggest adding a color word.

learn.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Share your own "Me" connection first, in under 30 seconds, to show the depth you want.
Point to the sentence starter when a girl gets stuck.
If you hear "she's a woman like me," ask what about her path stands out.

tryit.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: After each video pause, ask one question: "What did the video just say AI uses to learn?"
Let girls disagree on "Is it intelligent?" You don't need to settle it.
For MusicFX, offer one prompt shape: "[Genre] song with [instrument] in the style of [artist]."

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Give two quiet minutes to write before anyone talks.
Ask for volunteers on the last question. Don't call on anyone for it.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Expect high energy in MusicFX and a dip during Marmoset. Use the Hype Squad to bridge it.
Girls will want to skip the mind map. Don't let them: the mind map is the prompt engineering.
Show 2 or 3 Marmoset examples on the projector before girls explore.
Tracks that miss the genre are useful. They teach prompting.

warmup.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Accept any wording during the recall.
If a crew is stuck, give a starter: "AI learns by looking at lots of ___."
Keep a simple sheet of who has held each role.

learn.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Say: "Computers can't hear music, so people give them words to describe it."
Show 2 or 3 Marmoset searches before girls explore.
Think out loud while you build the prompt, mistakes included.

tryit.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Check mind maps at the 5-minute mark. If one is blank, fill it in together: "What instruments do you hear?"
For the Afrobeats map, offer starter words: drums, percussion, energetic, joyful, building. Girls add one of their own.
Mind map before MusicFX, every round.

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Write KEEP / TRY / CHANGE on the board.
If a girl is stuck, offer: "Keep the drums. Try a faster tempo. Change the mood word from chill to energetic."

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Build a sample model yourself before class. It takes 10 minutes.
Webcams fail? Switch to the Image Project and train on photos.
Push crews for variety: one dancer in one outfit means the model only knows her.
Watch for crews training on faces instead of poses.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Stuck crews: "AI is great at dogs because there are millions of dog photos online. It's bad at left-handed scissors because nobody photographs them."
Don't explain bias yet. Let the examples sit.

learn.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Say "examples" instead of "samples" and "groups" instead of "classes."
Explain the percentage: "The AI is guessing, and it tells you how sure it is."
Walk through every button on screen.

tryit.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: At 10 minutes, check sample counts. Under 20 per move? Add 10 more with a different dancer.
Catch crews training on faces instead of poses.
When the model guesses wrong, ask: "What does the AI think this is? Why?"

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Stay with their own example: "If your AI only saw one person dancing, it wouldn't recognize anyone else."
Then connect it: the same thing happens when face recognition is trained on one kind of face.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Your energy sets the tone. This is a celebration, not a test.
Announce each crew yourself and lead the clap-in.
Keep transitions between crews under 30 seconds.
Celebrate every crew equally, mistakes included.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Let each crew pick its own performance length.
Keep the brief on the board all lesson.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Offer 3 shapes: everyone in unison; a solo, then the crew joins one by one; or two pairs doing call-and-response.
Coach in four steps: pick moves, practice slowly, add the music, practice the order.

tryit.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Announce each crew and lead the clap-in.
If a Speaker freezes on the AI part, prompt: "Tell us one prompt word your crew used."
If she freezes on the intro: "Tell us your crew name."

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Put sentence starters on the board for the reflection form.
Keep it celebratory. Every girl stands for her role.

plan.title: 4 tips for your first time
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Expect high energy at the start, a dip during the algorithm math, then a lift at Canva. Use the Hype Squad to bridge the dip.
Make the math concrete: "100 likes but 50 angry emojis. Which algorithm pushes it harder?"
Girls who skip social media have a valuable outside view. Say so.
Canva can swallow time. Hold the 20-minute limit.

warmup.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Tell girls what to listen for before you press play.
Let girls name content they love, then steer the talk to patterns, not posts.
If a girl doesn't post, ask why her friends share what they share.

learn.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Walk one case study out loud first: what happened, why share it, how it feels, where the surprise is.
If the Algorithm 2 idea doesn't land, try this: "50 angry comments, or 50 quiet likes. Which post wins?"
Ask for real examples of a feed narrowing or widening someone's view.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Suggest a layout: title, three points, one picture per point, one closing line.
Ask for one specific fact. "Algorithms can be harmful" isn't enough. How?

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Keep each round to 4 minutes with a timer.
Hand out sticky notes before the walk starts, not during.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Energy runs very high during dancing and lower during the TikTok video. Use the Hype Squad to bridge.
Give credit: Reggaeton comes from Puerto Rico and Panama. Don't let the moves lose their roots.
Always offer the gentler version of el perreo first, and use consent language.
Point "I want to be famous" talk back to the project question.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Dance with them. Don't perform: take part.
You don't need to be good. Your job is to show the room is safe to dance in.

learn.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Sum up the rest of the TikTok video in your own words. Three sentences is plenty.
Try framing it both ways: computers help us find new music, and computers might choose for us.
Beat out the dembow on a table: boom, ch, boom, chick.

tryit.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Trust the tutorial videos. Keep crews on them and encourage.
Validate the gentler versions out loud.
Use dance words if you know them: isolation, weight transfer, hip hinge.

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Offer three ways to open a video: a question, a surprising fact or a striking picture.
Push for one concrete change, not a general wish.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: This is the newest lesson. Walk through the card sort and Teachable Machine yourself first, even if you've taught before.
Let girls set likes to 10. Then let the feed show them what happens.
Some girls will ask why this matters. Connect it to their own feed: what if it's making you anxious or angry?
Stay open to disagreement. There's no single right answer here.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Ask: "You said you want less news. Have you tried to change that?"
Girls without social media can describe a friend's feed.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Work one example on the board: 100 likes at weight 1 plus 50 comments at weight 5 scores 350.
Say it plainly: platforms chose these weights.

tryit.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Have crews agree on the goal before anyone sets a weight.
Walk one crew through the classifier, then let other crews copy.
Ask: "Could someone else label this post differently?"

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Use the recipe again: taste, health or speed. Which cake would you bake?
Write the "2 changes" answers where everyone can see them.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Your energy sets the tone. This is a celebration, not a test.
Draw names for the showcase order.
Have a backup: if filming fails, crews perform live.
This lesson works best in one block. If you must split it, break after filming.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Keep roles the same all lesson so crews can focus.
Write the brief on the board so crews can check it while they film.

learn.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Offer three openings: a surprising statement, one striking move, or a question.
Step in only if a video will miss the brief. Ask, "Where does the audience hear your message?"
Push for one full take early, then reshoot.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Hype each crew briefly before its premiere.
Let girls answer audience questions before you do.

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Give three quiet minutes to write before anyone shares.
Name what each girl did when you hand out her sticker.

plan.title: 4 tips for your first time
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Share your own hoop struggle first. It gives girls permission to be beginners.
Celebrate effort over skill during the Hoop Challenge.
Centripetal force is the big moment. Slow down and let it land.
Protect Reflect, even if you run behind.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Read the role scripts word for word the first time.
Keep your own hoop story under 30 seconds.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: At 3 minutes, point to the data sheet and ask, "What number goes in this box?"
Say "push" if "centripetal" feels like too much. It's the scientist's word for the inward push.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Offer arm hooping or partner hooping to anyone who struggles.
Let every girl choose her own level.

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Give quiet writing time before anyone shares.
Save the "1 question" answers to open Lesson 2.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Test the oscilloscope and microphone permission before class.
Keep the science talk short. The sliders do the teaching.
Pair up girls if a device fails.
Energy dips during the science. Use the Hype Squad.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Use thumbs up or sideways to check who's sure of the instrument.
Push girls to try a new role today.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Move one slider at a time.
Skip "Hz" if it feels like too much. Say "faster wiggles, higher sound."

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Give every crew the same four starting sounds: loud, quiet, high, low.
Keep the drum questions open. There are many right answers.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Ask what instrument they'd design. It sets up Lesson 3.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Set the quiet signal before building starts.
No building without an approved plan.
Run testing in set windows so you keep control of the room.
Set out trash bags for scraps.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Let crews pick drum, shaker or both on their own.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Use three steps: plan, build, test, improve.
Post the science word bank where everyone can see it.

tryit.title: 3 tips for this step
tips: Walk the room every 5 minutes.
Offer one suggestion, then step back.
Use finger-tap testing at first to keep the noise down.

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Lead applause after every demo.
Decide where instruments live until the Showcase.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Your energy sets the tone. Rehearsal can feel chaotic, and that's normal.
Have backup supplies for broken instruments.
Check in at 15 and 30 minutes.
Let crews keep their performance roles for the Showcase.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Offer three routine shapes if a crew is stuck.

learn.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Cap instrument fixes at 15 minutes.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: By 30 minutes, every crew should be running the routine.
Ask, "Where does the audience hear the science?"

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Use the same feedback pattern for every crew: one win, one polish, one hype line.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: This is a celebration, not a test.
Draw the performance order ahead of time.
Have a plan if a crew freezes.
Lead applause after every crew, equally.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Give a 2-minute warning before the show starts.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Announce each crew yourself.
Keep changeovers under 30 seconds.

tryit.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Offer sentence starters to girls who get stuck.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Name what each girl did as you hand out her sticker.

plan.title: 4 tips for your first time
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Linger on "How does it know?" after the game. Don't rush to the answer.
Use the dog example if "machine learning" feels big.
The moment the model gets fooled is the best teaching moment. Name it.
Make sure every crew leaves with its Pose Cards.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Take the full 8 minutes for roles in Lesson 1.
Receive every theory without correcting it.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Stay with the dog example. That's enough.
If the video runs over, cut the share-out, not the notes.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Give stuck crews the starter card: Hand Up, one hand above the head, left, right or both, close and far.
Aim for 3 minutes per crew. Cards you don't reach go first in Lesson 2.

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Ask for the crew whose card was hardest to fool.
Spotlight Speakers keep the cards. They're the most important thing in this module.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Energy runs high from the B-Girl video on. Set hard timers.
Redirect power moves to clean, repeatable moves.
Let the most experienced dancer be Movement Captain.
Hold girls in the writing. The card is the spec.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Stop the Sarah Bee clip at 3:11.
Accept simple labels. The real names come next.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Keep the history to 30 seconds, then ask the room.
Never ask one girl to speak for a community.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Use an 8-minute hard stop for choosing moves.
If a card is vague during recording, ask the crew to fix it out loud.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Check that every Spotlight Speaker has all 3 cards.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: The first version of any Pose Card is a draft. Say so.
Keep a visible timer so crews know when they're up.
Protect the outsider test.
The break is real. Don't skip it.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Name any partial answer as right.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Ask "Which angles?" when a card says "different angles."
Short on time? Drop to 4 minutes per crew and test later.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Ask, "What did the model get wrong? What didn't the card say?"
When the outsider fails, say it isn't the crew's fault. The model did what it learned.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Check every crew's 3 labeled cards before lanyards come off.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Your energy sets the tone. Hype it from the first second.
No cards, no cypher. Check every Spotlight Speaker.
Brief the audience fully. It keeps the scoring sharp.
Don't let the cypher run long.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: A simple clap-stomp beat is enough.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Practice the sample row twice with the audience.
Your only job during the cypher is energy: "Big applause! Next up..."

tryit.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Let the Hype Squad present every award.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Start the surveys on time so girls finish before lanyards come off.

plan.title: 4 tips for your first time
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: No girl has to share her number.
If a girl says this is pointless, agree that one person can't fix it alone, then point to the Showcase: her message reaches people.
When girls see their number, pause and let the silence sit.
Push commitments to be specific.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Take the full 8 minutes for roles in Lesson 1.
Lead the take-up-space move with full energy.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Use the balloon picture if CO2e feels abstract.
Say "16 vs. 4" twice. It's the number they'll use later.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Say, "This isn't a leaderboard."
Don't moralize about flights or meat. Move on.

reflect.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Cheer specific commitments loudly.
Every girl keeps her Commitment Card for Lesson 5.

plan.title: 3 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Name the lineage clearly and with respect.
Encourage volume. Quiet step isn't step.
Tell girls the clips are advanced. Today is the foundation.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Model loud, then soft, if crews are shy.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: You don't need to name all nine organizations. Trust the video.
Chant the four elements like a list until it sticks.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Lead slow before fast.
Let crews demo just three rounds.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Ask which element felt strongest.

plan.title: 3 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Protect the chant writing time.
Push past slogans: what does your chant say that no other crew's would?
Climate worry may come up. Put it into the words.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Write down every phrase, even the odd ones.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Start from the phrase list, not a blank page.
Offer the four-line frame at 10 minutes, not before.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Four or five moves is plenty.
Ask, "Does the move match the meaning of the line?"

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Applause only. Feedback comes in Lesson 4.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: The work is in the reps. Don't over-teach.
One fix per crew. Specific beats complete.
Plan a Hype Squad pump-up mid-class.
Watching yourself dance feels weird at first. Say so.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Let crews rebuild from the Planning Sheet.

learn.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Stay out of the way. Take notes for Cycle 2.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Pick from the one-fix list if you're unsure: volume, sync, hit-line intensity, eye contact or a strong start.
Keep waiting crews rehearsing.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Share Showcase details in writing too.

plan.title: 4 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Arrive early and test the sound.
Brief the audience: they cheer, not just clap.
Have the freeze script ready.
Protect the last 10 minutes.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Keep roles fixed all lesson.

learn.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Announce every crew yourself.
Lead applause after every crew.

tryit.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Read audience comments that name a line or a number.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Start the survey on time so girls finish before lanyards come off.

plan.title: 4 tips for your first time
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Pre-cut every bottle before class.
Give the model build its full 40 minutes.
Don't answer the opening question. Let the video do it.
Keep breathing exercises optional.

warmup.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Take the full 8 minutes for roles in Lesson 1.
Write every answer on the board, right or wrong.

learn.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Cross off and circle. That comparison is the lesson.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Play the whole build video before anyone starts.
Sticky tac fixes most straw problems.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: The gallery walk is learning time, not cleanup time. Keep both groups moving.

plan.title: 3 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Model counting one breath before the experiment.
Test MetaChart.com before class.
Protect the hypothesis step.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Push girls into roles they haven't had yet.

learn.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Use the team picture: heart and lungs working together.

tryit.title: 2 tips for this step
tips: Check each group's data table at 5 minutes.
Chart paper works if MetaChart fails.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Save the Mae Jemison video for groups that finish early.

plan.title: 3 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Set a safe tone before the content starts.
Frame the straw as a picture, not a test.
You don't need to fix it. Hold the space.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Hand out straws without explaining. Let the dance do it.

learn.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Start with the cars slider, then try rain.

tryit.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Ask how the source connects to last lesson's experiment.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Make sure every group agrees on the same song version.

plan.title: 3 tips for this lesson
plan.sub: For volunteers and first-time facilitators. STEM teachers can skip ahead.
tips: Never skip the storyboard.
Use the timer so you don't have to.
Pair weaker groups with stronger ones for the peer check.

warmup.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Let the whole song play.

learn.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Every group checks in before building.

tryit.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: Send drifting groups back to the storyboard.

reflect.title: 1 tip for this step
tips: A group can present its storyboard out loud if it truly isn't ready.
